name: Find Google Maps leads with SerpAPI, score them with OpenAI and send personal emails with Gmail

parameters.content:
## Find Google Maps leads with SerpAPI, score them with OpenAI and send personal emails with Gmail

### How it works
1. Every morning, each "keyword | location" line becomes a Google Maps search through SerpAPI.
2. New businesses are deduplicated against the sheet, and their websites are read for emails, Instagram and what they do.
3. OpenAI scores each lead against your ideal customer and finds a personal opening line. Leads are saved to Google Sheets and you get a summary.
4. On weekdays, a few emails per hour go out from Gmail: first emails to the best new leads, follow-ups in the same thread.
5. Replies stop the sequence, and "stop" replies mark the lead as opted out.

### Setup steps
- [ ] Add **SerpAPI**, **OpenAI**, **Google Sheets** and **Gmail** credentials.
- [ ] Create a spreadsheet with empty `Leads` and `Error Log` tabs and select it in every Google Sheets node.
- [ ] Edit **Prospecting Settings** (searches, ideal customer, offer) and **Outreach Settings** (sender, volume).
- [ ] Set the workflow time zone, then activate.

### Customization
Change the scoring rules in **Score Lead** and the email style in **Write Email**.

## Plan the searches
Known leads are loaded so nobody is found twice.

## Find new businesses
Google Maps via SerpAPI, then each website.

## Score each lead with AI
Fit score, summary and an opening hook.

## Save and report
Appends the leads and emails a summary.

## Plan the hourly outreach
Replies first, then follow-ups and new leads.

## Record replies
Stops the sequence for leads who answered.

## Write the email with AI
One lead at a time, in the lead’s language.

## Send and track
Follow-ups reply in the same thread.

## Catch workflow errors
Builds an incident report from any failed execution.

## Send the alert
Emails it, or logs it to the Error Log tab.

nodes.name: Every Day at 07:00
nodes.notes: Uses the workflow time zone (Settings → Timezone).

assignments.name: searches
assignments.value:
dental clinic | Jakarta Selatan

assignments.name: ideal_customer
assignments.value: Owner-led small and medium businesses (5–50 people) that sell to consumers and still take orders or bookings by WhatsApp or phone.

assignments.name: offer
assignments.value: We set up WhatsApp booking assistants that answer customers 24/7 and fill the calendar.

nodes.name: Prospecting Settings
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. searches: one "keyword | location" per line; each line is one SerpAPI search with up to 20 businesses. Add more lines (for example per district) to find more leads. ideal_customer and offer drive the AI score and the emails.

nodes.name: Read Lead Sheet
nodes.notes: Every lead found so far. Used to skip businesses and domains that are already in the sheet.

assignments.name: jobs
assignments.value: ={{ String($('Prospecting Settings').first().json.searches).split('\n').map(l => l.split('|').map(s => s.trim())).filter(p => p[0]).map(([keyword, location]) => ({ q: location ? keyword + ' ' + location : keyword, keyword, location: location || '' })) }}

nodes.name: Build Search Jobs
nodes.notes: One job per line of the searches setting.

nodes.name: Search Google Maps
nodes.notes: One SerpAPI search per line (up to 20 places each), one per second. A failed search is counted in the daily summary instead of stopping the run. No Retry On Fail: n8n would repeat every search of the run, not just the failed one.

nodes.name: Collect New Places
nodes.notes: Dedupes by Google place ID and by website domain, inside this run and against the sheet. Caps the run at max_new_leads_per_run.

nodes.name: Read Websites
nodes.notes: Five sites at a time, 12 s timeout each. When the homepage has no email it tries the first contact page it links to.

messageValues.message:
=You qualify B2B leads for this offer: {{ $('Prospecting Settings').first().json.offer }}
Ideal customer: {{ $('Prospecting Settings').first().json.ideal_customer }}

Score how well the business fits (0 = clearly not a fit, 100 = perfect fit). Judge only from the facts given; when the website is missing, be conservative.
- personalization_hook: one concrete, verifiable detail from the website or the listing to open an email with (a service, a location, a claim). Empty when there is none. Never invent details.
- best_email: the best address from "Emails found" to contact the owner or manager, or "" when none fits. Prefer named or generic business addresses on the company domain over personal webmail.
- email_language: the language of the website, "Indonesian" or "English".
Return only JSON matching the schema.

nodes.name: Score Lead
nodes.notes: One short AI call per new lead, five in parallel. A failed call gives the lead score 0 and the reason, so it is still saved.

nodes.name: OpenAI · Scoring Model
nodes.notes: Low reasoning effort is enough for scoring. Max Retries handles 429 / 5xx.

nodes.name: Lead Score Schema
nodes.notes: autoFix repairs malformed JSON once with the fixer model.

nodes.name: OpenAI · Scoring Fixer
nodes.notes: Only called when the model returns JSON that does not match Lead Score Schema. "Use Responses API" is off on purpose: the auto-fix step reads this model's reply as plain text.

assignments.name: Email
assignments.value: ={{ (() => { const o = $json.output; const found = $('Read Websites').item.json.site.emails; return o?.best_email && found.includes(o.best_email.toLowerCase()) ? o.best_email.toLowerCase() : (found[0] || ''); })() }}

assignments.name: Status

nodes.name: Build Lead Row
nodes.notes: Field names = Leads sheet headers. Only "New" leads (fit and an email) are emailed. The email must be one the website actually shows, so the AI cannot invent an address.

nodes.name: Save Leads
nodes.notes: One append call for all new leads. Headers are created on an empty tab.

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Lead finder · ' + $('Build Lead Row').all().filter(i => i.json.Status === 'New').length + ' new leads ready for outreach' }}

nodes.name: Email Daily Summary
nodes.notes: Runs only when the run found new businesses.

nodes.name: Every Weekday Hour
nodes.notes: Weekdays at 09:05–16:05 (workflow time zone). Small hourly batches look like a person writing, not a blast.

assignments.name: offer
assignments.value: We set up WhatsApp booking assistants that answer customers 24/7 and fill the calendar.

assignments.name: call_to_action
assignments.value: Would a 15-minute call next week be useful?

assignments.name: stop_words
assignments.value: stop,unsubscribe,remove me,not interested,no thanks,berhenti,tidak tertarik,jangan kirim

nodes.name: Outreach Settings
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. 5 emails per hour × 8 hours = up to 40 per weekday per Gmail account, a safe volume for a warm mailbox. booking_link is optional.

nodes.name: Find Replies
nodes.notes: Inbox mail of the last 30 days. Replies stop the sequence; stop words mark the lead as opted out.

nodes.name: Read Leads
nodes.notes: The whole lead list. Fine for a few thousand rows; archive old rows beyond that.

nodes.name: Plan Outreach
nodes.notes: Follow-ups go first, then the best-scoring new leads, within emails_per_hour. Leads that replied are never emailed again.

nodes.name: Mark Replied
nodes.notes: Replied leads are yours to answer in Gmail; the workflow stops emailing them.

nodes.name: Loop Over Leads
nodes.notes: One lead per pass: a retried Gmail send then only repeats that lead, never the whole batch.

messageValues.message:
=You write short, personal B2B emails for {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.sender_name }} from {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.sender_company }}.
Offer: {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.offer }}

Rules:
- Write in the requested language. Plain text, no markdown, no emojis, no links except {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.booking_link || 'none (do not add links)' }}.
- First email: subject under 7 words, body 60–110 words. Open with the personalization hook in your own words (skip it if it is "none"), connect it to one problem the offer solves, end with this call to action: {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.call_to_action }}
- Follow-up: body 25–50 words, friendly, adds one new reason, same call to action. Subject is ignored (it is sent as a reply in the same thread).
- Never claim to have used their product, never invent facts, numbers or clients.
- Sign with {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.sender_name }}, {{ $('Outreach Settings').first().json.sender_company }}.
- Add one last line saying they can reply "stop" and you will not email again (in the same language).
Return only JSON matching the schema.

nodes.name: Write Email
nodes.notes: Writes both first emails and follow-ups. A failed call skips that lead this hour (no email is sent).

nodes.name: OpenAI · Writing Model
nodes.notes: Max Retries handles 429 / 5xx.

nodes.name: Email Schema
nodes.notes: Subject and plain-text body.

nodes.name: OpenAI · Writing Fixer
nodes.notes: Only called when the model returns JSON that does not match Email Schema. "Use Responses API" is off on purpose: the auto-fix step reads this model's reply as plain text.

nodes.name: Email Written?
nodes.notes: Skips leads whose email could not be written this hour; they are picked again next hour.

nodes.name: Send Follow-up
nodes.notes: Replies in the thread of the first email. "Reply to recipients only" keeps your own address out of the To field.

nodes.name: Send First Email
nodes.notes: Plain text, no tracking pixel: it reads like a personal email.

nodes.name: Mark Followed Up
nodes.notes: "Followed up" ends the sequence once max_followups is reached; a reply still marks the lead Replied.

nodes.name: Mark Contacted
nodes.notes: Stores the Gmail message ID so the follow-up lands in the same thread.

nodes.name: On Workflow Error
nodes.notes: Internal error workflow: n8n starts here when any production execution of THIS workflow fails (and Settings → Error workflow is empty).

nodes.name: Alert Settings
nodes.notes: EDIT ME. Who gets incident alerts. Comma-separate multiple emails.

assignments.name: severity
error_message
assignments.value: ={{ String($('On Workflow Error').first().json.execution?.error?.message ?? $('On Workflow Error').first().json.trigger?.error?.message ?? 'No error message provided').slice(0, 2000) }}

nodes.name: Build Incident Report
nodes.notes: Normalises the Error Trigger payload (execution errors and trigger errors have different shapes) into one incident record.

Next step: open the failed execution, check the input of the failed node, fix the cause, then use Retry → From failed node in the Executions list.

nodes.name: Email Alert
nodes.notes: Primary alert. Email is independent of the services this workflow calls, so their outage cannot silence the alert. Retries 3× / 5 s, then the fallback runs.

nodes.name: Error Log Row
nodes.notes: Shapes the Error Log columns and renames the email failure reason. Keeps a field called 'error' away from the Sheets node: Retry On Fail treats an output item with 'error' as a failed try and would append the row again.

nodes.name: Fallback · Log to Error Sheet
nodes.notes: Only runs when the email alert failed after 3 tries. Appends the incident to the 'Error Log' tab; the header row is created on first use. If this fails too, the error run shows as failed in Executions.
